```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhu_2024_infliximab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhu_2024_infliximab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2024.1430120> (open access)
* Supplement: Supplementary Material (DOCX) with the final parameter table
  (Table S5), the covariate bootstrap (Table S3) and the backward-elimination
  table (Table S4).

Zhu et al. related early infliximab trough levels and antibodies to infliximab
(ATI) to clinical remission at week 14 in Chinese patients with Crohn's
disease, then used a population PK model fitted to 526 samples from 140
patients to simulate the probability of reaching the week-2 trough target of
20.08 ug/mL across induction doses, body weights and albumin levels. The PK
model is one-compartment with first-order elimination after IV infusion:

$$V = 9.65 \times \frac{FFM}{56.1}$$

$$CL = \theta_{ATI} \times 0.45 \times \left(\frac{FFM}{56.1}\right)^{0.75} \times \left(\frac{ALB}{40}\right)^{-0.48}$$

with $\theta_{ATI}$ = 1 for ATI absent or titre 1:20, 1.17 for titre 1:60 and
1.38 for titre >= 1:180.

# Population

The model was developed in 140 patients with Crohn's disease treated at the
First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University, China, between October 2020
and December 2022 (Table 1): 106 men and 34 women, median age 34 years (range
15-58), mean weight 59.9 kg (SD 10.8, range 39-80), median baseline albumin
38.3 g/L (IQR 34.4-43.1). Induction doses were 200 mg (19 patients), 300 mg
(105) or 400 mg (16) at weeks 0, 2 and 6, then every 8 weeks. ATI were
detected in 234 of 526 samples (1:20 in 96, 1:60 in 86, >= 1:180 in 52), and
66 samples (12.6%) were below the 0.50 ug/mL quantification limit, almost all
from ATI-positive patients.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Zhu_2024_infliximab")$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|------:|-----------------|
| One-compartment, first-order elimination | n/a | Results, "Modelling" |
| `lcl` (CL, reference patient) | 0.45 L/day | Table S5; Eq. 4 |
| `lvc` (V, reference patient) | 9.65 L | Table S5; Eq. 3 |
| `e_ffm_cl` (FFM exponent on CL, reference 56.1 kg) | 0.75 (fixed) | Eq. 4 |
| `e_ffm_vc` (FFM exponent on V, reference 56.1 kg) | 1 (fixed) | Eq. 3 |
| `e_alb_cl` (albumin exponent on CL, reference 40 g/L) | -0.48 | Table S5; Eq. 4 |
| `e_ada60_cl` (CL factor, ATI titre 1:60) | 1.17 | Table S5; Eq. 4 |
| `e_ada180_cl` (CL factor, ATI titre >= 1:180) | 1.38 | Table S5; Eq. 4 |
| `etalcl` (IIV on CL) | 25.1% CV, variance 0.0611 | Table S5 |
| `propSd` | 26.6% | Table S5 |
| `addSd` | 0.15 ug/mL | Table S5 |
| FFM from weight, height and sex | Janmahasatian 2005 | Methods, "popPK modelling" |
| Exponential IIV; combined proportional + additive error | n/a | Methods, "popPK modelling" |

# Fat-free mass

The model takes fat-free mass directly. The helper below applies the
Janmahasatian formula the authors cite.

```{r ffm-helper}
janmahasatian_ffm <- function(wt_kg, ht_cm, sexf) {
  bmi <- wt_kg / (ht_cm / 100)^2
  # rep_len() so a scalar sex or height still returns one FFM per weight
  ifelse(
    rep_len(sexf, length(bmi)) == 1,
    9270 * wt_kg / (8780 + 244 * bmi),
    9270 * wt_kg / (6680 + 216 * bmi)
  )
}
```

# Typical-value profiles

The reference patient (FFM 56.1 kg, albumin 40 g/L) receives 300 mg at weeks
0, 2 and 6 and every 8 weeks thereafter, without ATI and at each ATI titre
class. With CL = 0.45 L/day and V = 9.65 L, the elimination half-life is
`log(2) * 9.65 / 0.45` = 14.9 days.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Zhu_2024_infliximab")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

dose_days <- c(0, 14, 42, seq(98, 378, by = 56))
obs_days <- seq(0, 378, by = 1)

ati_levels <- tibble(
  id = 1:4,
  ADA_TITER = c(0, 20, 60, 180),
  ati = factor(
    c("absent", "1:20", "1:60", ">=1:180"),
    levels = c("absent", "1:20", "1:60", ">=1:180")
  )
)

ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  expand_grid(ati_levels, time = dose_days) |>
    mutate(amt = 300, evid = 1L),
  expand_grid(ati_levels, time = obs_days) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", FFM = 56.1, ALB = 40) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_typ, keep = "ati") |>
  as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time / 7, Cc, colour = ati)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)",
    y = "Infliximab (ug/mL)",
    colour = "ATI titre",
    title = "Typical reference patient, 300 mg at weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

ATI titres of 1:60 and >= 1:180 raise clearance by 17% and 38%; the 1:20
class shares the reference clearance, so its curve overlies the ATI-absent
one.

```{r typical-check}
trough_typ <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time %in% c(13, 41, 97)) |>
  select(ati, time, Cc) |>
  mutate(week = (time + 1) / 7)

kel_ref <- 0.45 / 9.65
c_wk2_closed <- 300 / 9.65 * exp(-kel_ref * 13)
c_wk2_sim <- trough_typ$Cc[trough_typ$ati == "absent" & trough_typ$time == 13]
stopifnot(abs(c_wk2_sim / c_wk2_closed - 1) < 1e-4)

trough_typ |>
  select(-time) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = week, values_from = Cc, names_prefix = "week_") |>
  rename(
    "ATI titre" = ati,
    "Trough week 2 (ug/mL)" = week_2,
    "Trough week 6 (ug/mL)" = week_6,
    "Trough week 14 (ug/mL)" = week_14
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Virtual cohort and induction troughs

A cohort resembling Table 1 receives the dose mix of the study (14% 200 mg,
75% 300 mg, 11% 400 mg) at weeks 0, 2 and 6. Weight is drawn from a normal
distribution with the Table 1 mean and SD truncated to its range, 24% of
subjects are women, and baseline albumin is log-normal with the Table 1 median
and IQR. Heights are 170 cm (SD 6) for men and 158 cm (SD 5) for women; see
"Assumptions and deviations" for why the Table 1 height is not used. All
subjects are ATI-absent, which is how the week-2 target was simulated in the
paper.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2024)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2024)

n_sub <- 200
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 34 / 140),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 59.9, 10.8), 39), 80),
  HT = ifelse(SEXF == 1, rnorm(n_sub, 158, 5), rnorm(n_sub, 170, 6)),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(38.3), 0.167), 27.5), 53.1),
  dose = sample(c(200, 300, 400), n_sub, replace = TRUE, prob = c(19, 105, 16) / 140),
  ADA_TITER = 0
) |>
  mutate(
    FFM = janmahasatian_ffm(WT, HT, SEXF),
    treatment = paste(dose, "mg")
  )

summary(cohort$FFM)

trough_days <- c(13.99, 41.99, 97.99)
ev_cohort <- bind_rows(
  expand_grid(cohort, time = c(0, 14, 42)) |>
    mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L),
  expand_grid(cohort, time = sort(c(seq(0, 98, by = 1), trough_days))) |>
    mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_cohort <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_cohort, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r cohort-plot}
sim_cohort |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = median(sim),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "purple") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 20.08, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)",
    y = "Infliximab (ug/mL)",
    title = "Simulated induction, Table 1-like cohort (median and 90% interval)",
    caption = "Compare with the early bins of Figure 4 of Zhu 2024. Dashed line: week-2 target 20.08 ug/mL."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper reports median troughs only within the 43-patient remission cohort,
split by outcome (Results, "Early induction IFX level"): week 2, 23.65 vs
16.96 ug/mL; week 6, 19.21 vs 11.18 ug/mL; week 14, 5.63 vs 2.21 ug/mL in
patients with and without remission (29 and 14 patients). The simulated
whole-cohort median is compared with the midpoint of the two group medians at
weeks 2 and 6; it lands near the no-remission median, about 10-15% below the
midpoint, and since two-thirds of the observed cohort were in remission the
observed whole-cohort median is likely above the midpoint. Part of the gap
plausibly reflects the assumed heights (a taller cohort has more fat-free
mass and lower concentrations). Week 14 is not compared because the observed
values include the ATI that a quarter of patients had developed by then
(Figure 3A), which this ATI-absent simulation omits.

```{r cohort-troughs}
trough_sim <- sim_cohort |>
  filter(time %in% trough_days[1:2]) |>
  mutate(week = round((time + 0.01) / 7)) |>
  group_by(week) |>
  summarise(
    median_sim = median(sim),
    q25 = quantile(sim, 0.25),
    q75 = quantile(sim, 0.75),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    median_remission = c(23.65, 19.21),
    median_no_remission = c(16.96, 11.18)
  )

trough_sim |>
  rename(
    "Week" = week,
    "Simulated median (ug/mL)" = median_sim,
    "Simulated Q1" = q25,
    "Simulated Q3" = q75,
    "Observed median, remission" = median_remission,
    "Observed median, no remission" = median_no_remission
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# A wrong volume, dose or unit moves the median by far more than 30%;
# across seeds the realised gap to the midpoint was -10% to -15%.
midpoint <- (trough_sim$median_remission + trough_sim$median_no_remission) / 2
stopifnot(all(abs(trough_sim$median_sim / midpoint - 1) < 0.3))
```

# Replicating Figure 5: week-2 target attainment

Figure 5 shows the probability that the week-2 trough (immediately before the
second infusion) exceeds 20.08 ug/mL after a single induction dose of
200-700 mg, by body weight (45-70 kg) and albumin (30, 35, 40 and 45 g/L), in
ATI-absent patients, with 1,000 virtual patients per point. The paper states
neither the height nor the sex used to turn weight into fat-free mass; the
simulation below uses men (76% of the cohort) 170 cm tall. The target is applied to the simulated
observation (`sim`, including residual error). The values in `fig5` were read
from the figure by the maintainers.

```{r fig5-digitised}
fig5 <- tribble(
  ~ALB, ~dose, ~WT, ~pta_paper,
  30, 200, 45, 5, 30, 200, 50, 2, 30, 200, 55, 1,
  30, 300, 45, 40, 30, 300, 50, 32, 30, 300, 55, 26, 30, 300, 60, 11, 30, 300, 65, 18, 30, 300, 70, 14,
  30, 400, 45, 71, 30, 400, 50, 66, 30, 400, 55, 61, 30, 400, 60, 55, 30, 400, 65, 51, 30, 400, 70, 48,
  30, 500, 45, 86, 30, 500, 50, 84, 30, 500, 55, 81, 30, 500, 60, 77, 30, 500, 65, 74, 30, 500, 70, 72,
  30, 600, 55, 89, 30, 600, 60, 88, 30, 600, 65, 85, 30, 600, 70, 84,
  30, 700, 65, 92, 30, 700, 70, 91,
  35, 200, 45, 8, 35, 200, 50, 5, 35, 200, 55, 3,
  35, 300, 45, 46, 35, 300, 50, 37, 35, 300, 55, 33, 35, 300, 60, 26, 35, 300, 65, 22, 35, 300, 70, 19,
  35, 400, 45, 75, 35, 400, 50, 72, 35, 400, 55, 67, 35, 400, 60, 62, 35, 400, 65, 57, 35, 400, 70, 53,
  35, 500, 45, 89, 35, 500, 50, 86, 35, 500, 55, 83, 35, 500, 60, 81, 35, 500, 65, 79, 35, 500, 70, 76,
  35, 600, 55, 91, 35, 600, 60, 89, 35, 600, 65, 88, 35, 600, 70, 87,
  35, 700, 65, 93, 35, 700, 70, 93,
  40, 200, 45, 9, 40, 200, 50, 7, 40, 200, 55, 4,
  40, 300, 45, 52, 40, 300, 50, 45, 40, 300, 55, 39, 40, 300, 60, 32, 40, 300, 65, 27, 40, 300, 70, 22,
  40, 400, 45, 80, 40, 400, 50, 75, 40, 400, 55, 72, 40, 400, 60, 66, 40, 400, 65, 63, 40, 400, 70, 58,
```

Each of the `r nrow(fig5)` scenarios is simulated with 200 virtual patients
(the paper used 1,000), so a single simulated probability carries a Monte
Carlo standard error of up to 3.5 percentage points.

```{r fig5-sim}
n_per_arm <- 200
pta_ids <- fig5 |>
  mutate(arm = row_number()) |>
  expand_grid(rep = seq_len(n_per_arm)) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    FFM = janmahasatian_ffm(WT, 170, 0),
    ADA_TITER = 0
  )

ev_pta <- bind_rows(
  pta_ids |> mutate(time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L),
  pta_ids |> mutate(time = 13.99, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_pta <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_pta, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame()

pta_sim <- sim_pta |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(pta_sim = 100 * mean(sim > 20.08), .groups = "drop")

pta_cmp <- fig5 |>
  mutate(arm = row_number()) |>
  left_join(pta_sim, by = "arm") |>
  mutate(diff = pta_sim - pta_paper)
```

```{r fig5-plot, fig.height = 6}
pta_cmp |>
  pivot_longer(c(pta_paper, pta_sim), names_to = "source", values_to = "pta") |>
  mutate(
    source = recode(source, pta_paper = "Zhu 2024 Figure 5", pta_sim = "This model"),
    dose = factor(paste(dose, "mg"), levels = paste(seq(200, 700, 100), "mg")),
    ALB = paste("Albumin", ALB, "g/L")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(WT, pta, colour = dose, linetype = source, shape = source)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(50, 80), colour = "grey50", linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~ALB) +
  labs(
    x = "Body weight (kg)",
    y = "Probability of week-2 trough > 20.08 ug/mL (%)",
    colour = "Dose",
    linetype = NULL,
    shape = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Zhu 2024."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig5-check}
pta_cmp |>
  summarise(
    median_abs_diff = median(abs(diff)),
    p90_abs_diff = quantile(abs(diff), 0.9),
    max_abs_diff = max(abs(diff))
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Median |difference| (points)" = median_abs_diff,
    "90th percentile |difference|" = p90_abs_diff,
    "Max |difference|" = max_abs_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# A wrong FFM exponent or reference moves the 70 kg points by 20-50
# percentage points (FFM taken equal to weight gives about 6% instead of
# the printed 22% at 300 mg, 70 kg, 40 g/L). With 200-subject Monte Carlo
# noise and figure reading, the 90th percentile of |difference| was 4.0-4.7
# over four seeds; single points reached 14.5.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(pta_cmp$diff)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(pta_cmp$diff), 0.9) < 12
)
```

The model reproduces Figure 5 across all four albumin panels. One printed
point is out of line with its neighbours: 300 mg at 60 kg and 30 g/L reads 11%
in the figure, below the 65 kg (18%) and 70 kg (14%) points, while clearance
and volume change smoothly with weight; the model gives a value between the 55
kg and 65 kg points, as a smooth curve would.

# Height sensitivity of the Figure 5 replication

Table 1 prints a mean height of 158.5 cm (SD 4.95, range 150-188), which is
low for a cohort that is 76% male and hard to reconcile with an SD of 5 cm
and a maximum of 188 cm. With 158.5 cm, FFM at a given weight is about 2 kg
smaller and the typical week-2 trough about 4-5% higher:

```{r height-sensitivity}
typ_c14 <- function(dose, wt, alb, ht) {
  ffm <- janmahasatian_ffm(wt, ht, 0)
  cl <- 0.45 * (ffm / 56.1)^0.75 * (alb / 40)^-0.48
  v <- 9.65 * ffm / 56.1
  dose / v * exp(-cl / v * 13.99)
}
tibble(height_cm = c(158.5, 170)) |>
  mutate(
    ffm_at_45kg = janmahasatian_ffm(45, height_cm, 0),
    typical_c14_300mg_45kg_alb40 = typ_c14(300, 45, 40, height_cm),
    typical_c14_300mg_70kg_alb40 = typ_c14(300, 70, 40, height_cm)
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Height (cm)" = height_cm,
    "FFM at 45 kg, male (kg)" = ffm_at_45kg,
    "Typical week-2 trough, 300 mg, 45 kg (ug/mL)" = typical_c14_300mg_45kg_alb40,
    "Typical week-2 trough, 300 mg, 70 kg (ug/mL)" = typical_c14_300mg_70kg_alb40
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

That raises target attainment by a few percentage points, the same order as
the Monte Carlo and digitisation noise in the comparison above, so Figure 5
cannot pin down the height the authors used. It does exclude using body
weight in place of FFM, which changes the 70 kg points by 20-50 percentage
points.

# PKNCA: single induction dose

Single 200, 300 and 400 mg doses in the reference patient (FFM 56.1 kg,
albumin 40 g/L, ATI absent), typical values. The paper reports no NCA, so the
half-life is checked against the closed-form one-compartment value.

```{r pknca}
nca_ids <- tibble(id = 1:3, dose = c(200, 300, 400)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose, "mg"))
nca_times <- c(0, 0.04, 0.25, 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42, 56, 70, 84, 112)
ev_nca <- bind_rows(
  nca_ids |> mutate(time = 0, amt = dose, evid = 1L),
  expand_grid(nca_ids, time = nca_times) |> mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", FFM = 56.1, ALB = 40, ADA_TITER = 0) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_nca, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  nca_ids |> mutate(time = 0),
  dose ~ time | treatment + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_tab |>
  rename(
    "Dose" = treatment,
    "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
    "AUC0-inf (ug*day/mL)" = aucinf.obs,
    "t1/2 (day)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

thalf_closed <- log(2) * 9.65 / 0.45
auc_closed <- nca_ids$dose / 0.45
stopifnot(
  all(abs(nca_tab$half.life / thalf_closed - 1) < 0.02),
  all(abs(nca_tab$aucinf.obs / auc_closed - 1) < 0.03)
)
```

The NCA half-life matches `log(2) * V / CL` = `r round(thalf_closed, 1)` days
and AUC0-inf matches dose / CL.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Height and sex in the Figure 5 simulation.** The paper simulates by body
  weight but the model is written in fat-free mass, and neither the height
  nor the sex behind the conversion is stated. Men 170 cm tall reproduce the
  figure; the Table 1 mean height of 158.5 cm gives target attainment a few
  percentage points higher (see the height-sensitivity section). The Table 1
  height looks misprinted for a cohort that is 76% male, so the virtual
  cohort above uses sex-specific heights (170 cm for men, 158 cm for women)
  rather than the printed value.
* **Residual error in the target-attainment simulation.** The target is
  applied to the simulated observation including residual error. Applied to
  the individual prediction (IIV only), attainment is lower at the 70 kg
  points than the figure shows, so the paper's simulation appears to include
  residual error even though the caption mentions only inter-patient
  variability.
* **FFM reference value.** The model normalises FFM to 56.1 kg. The
  Janmahasatian formula applied to the Table 1 demographics gives a median
  FFM nearer 47-50 kg, so 56.1 kg is not obviously the cohort median FFM; it
  is used as printed, and the Figure 5 replication confirms that the printed
  equations, with this reference, reproduce the authors' simulations.
* **Target value.** The Results and the ROC analysis give 20.08 ug/mL; the
  Figure 5 caption and the Discussion print 20.8 ug/mL. The replication uses
  20.08.
* **Covariate time dependence.** Albumin and ATI were screened as
  time-varying covariates and weight as both baseline and time-varying. The
  paper does not state which form of FFM entered the final model; the model
  accepts whatever FFM, ALB and ADA_TITER columns are supplied at each record.
* **ATI coding.** ATI titres are reported as absent, 1:20, 1:60 and
  >= 1:180. The model takes the reciprocal dilution in `ADA_TITER` (0 when
  absent) and applies the 1:60 factor for 60 <= `ADA_TITER` < 180 and the
  >= 1:180 factor from 180 upwards. Absent and 1:20 share the reference
  clearance, as in Eq. 4.
* **IIV.** Table S5 reports IIV on CL as 25.1%, read here as a CV and
  converted to a log-normal variance of log(0.251^2 + 1) = 0.0611. No IIV on
  V was reported.
* **Below-quantification samples** were handled with the M5 method in the
  original fit; this has no bearing on simulation.
* **Week-2 timing.** Troughs are taken at day 13.99, just before the second
  infusion; doses are given as boluses because infusion durations were not
  reported, which has a negligible effect on troughs two weeks later.
